clinician.trajectory_summary: 26-year-old postpartum woman (P4G1) presented following pregnancy termination at 30 weeks for fetal growth restriction/PPROM with fever, anemia, thrombocytopenia, AKI, and coagulopathy progressing to respiratory failure, DIC, and MODS requiring ICU transfer. Diagnostic workup revealed microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with fragmented red blood cells on peripheral smear (E005), decreased complement C3 and C4 indicating complement activation (E005), and negative blood/stool cultures, hepatitis B DNA, autoantibodies, and Coombs test excluding infectious and autoimmune etiologies (E005). Liver function tests showed AST/ALT elevations with disproportionate hyperbilirubinemia pattern consistent with hemolysis rather than HELLP syndrome (E002). The patient underwent nine sessions of plasma exchange with hemofiltration and blood transfusions, demonstrating clinical response with normalization of complement levels, platelet count, hemoglobin stability, and improved urine output to 1300 mL/day, confirmed by bone marrow biopsy showing resolution of fragmented red blood cells (E007). Despite absence of documented ADAMTS13 activity, Shiga toxin testing, or complement genetic studies in the source records, the clinical picture of postpartum-triggered thrombotic microangiopathy with hypocomplementemia and exclusion of secondary causes supported the confirmed diagnosis of aHUS (E005).
